maya: Heads-up: enabled the new precision-switcher FP8 kernel on the H100 canary fleet (~5 nodes) and L40S staging for model alexa-v2-lastmile. Running eval suite shows a small but consistent quality delta (+6% perplexity on Q2 prompts).
liam: Oof. When did this go live?
maya: rolled at 1729301200 via canary rollout policy. small traffic, but reproduceable in offline eval.
eva: Can you paste the eval numbers and command?
maya: eval summary:
```
model: alexa-v2-lastmile
device: h100-canary (fp8-kernel)
seq: 2048
metric: ppl
baseline (fp16): 12.8
fp8-enabled: 13.6
delta: +6.25%
```
maya: repro command: `python infra/evals/run_eval.py --model alexa-v2-lastmile --quant fp8 --device h100 --seq 2048 --seed 42`
liam: Any NaNs or runtime warnings in the logs?
maya: No NaNs in this run, but I saw saturation warnings in the kernel log earlier: `WARN: activation_scale overflow at layer 19` (small count). Also noticed slightly different tokenization on a tiny subset (weird).
nihal: Tokenization diff sounds odd — FP8 should not touch tokenizer. Could be nondeterministic batching order or KV cache alignment mismatch when we flip to the fp8 path.
liam: Agreed. Kernel-level tiling change could change ordering of ops and numerical rounding -> small distribution shift. Did we enable any fused attention/tiling changes with the fp8 path?
maya: yes, fp8 path uses tiled attention kernel and a different row-major packing for KV caches on H100. L40S compiled path uses another codegen. Both were supposed to be isomorphic but maybe not.
eva: Let's bisect: can we run the eval with `--force-serial` and `--no-tiling` flags to isolate tiling vs quantization?
maya: good idea. I'll run: `python infra/evals/run_eval.py --model alexa-v2-lastmile --quant fp8 --device h100 --seq 2048 --flags "--force-serial --disable-tiling"` and post results in 20m.
liam: Also run the fp8 runtime with `--canonical-scale-table` to ensure quant params are identical to offline calib.
nihal: If delta persists with tiling off and canonical scales on, then it's likely quant noise from low-bit mantissa rounding (FP8 e5m2 vs e4m3 differences).
sre-bot: Deploy: canary rollout progressed to 5/5 nodes for service alexa-inference (maya) at 1729302400
deploy-bot: Rollback suggestion: 1 failing canary check (quality regression) — open to manual rollback.
maya: Can we pause the canary? I prefer to freeze rollout while we bisect. @eva can you open a quick revert PR for the canary flag?
eva: Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/pr/3589 — will flip `enable_fp8_kernel_canary=false` for the canary pool.
liam: I'll start a short unit reproducer that toggles only the quant path (no tiling, same compute graph) and push logs. Might help catch activation scaling mismatch.
nihal: Also check calibration harness: did we reuse per-layer scales computed with the reference kernel or with the new tiled kernel? mismatch there would explain small but consistent bias.
maya: noted. action items: 1) run tiling-off serial eval (maya) 2) run canonical-scale fp8 eval (liam) 3) PR to pause canary (eva) 4) collect kernel logs w/ `ACT_SCALE` trace enabled (nihal).
liam: If anyone wants a quick local repro: `./scripts/quant_repro.sh alexa-v2-lastmile h100 fp8 2048` — it sets environment to `TF_ENABLE_TILING=0` and dumps scales.
maya: Will paste the follow-up results here. Thanks. :raised_hands:
(20 minutes later)
maya: Update: tiling off + canonical-scale -> ppl 12.82 (within noise). So tiling/packing differences look like the culprit.
nihal: Great find. So downstream: we need to reconcile packing conversions or add a normalization step when switching kernels. Also add regression test to the eval harness that runs a small subset with `--disable-tiling` and ensures <0.5% ppl delta.
eva: PR merged to pause canary. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3590 :white_check_mark:
liam: I'll prototype a compat shim that applies per-layer post-scale to KV cache on kernel switch and run microbench.
maya: filing ops ticket for a staged reenable plan once shim + tests exist. ticket: RW-OPS-1223
nihal: Also add a runtime flag to force the canonical packing for critical models until we validate.
maya: Perfect. Thanks team — nice bisect. :tada:
